newsitem.title: TURKEY: Kurdish rebels block Turkish road to Iraqi border.
newsitem.headline: Kurdish rebels block Turkish road to Iraqi border.

text.p: Separatist Kurdish rebels in southeast Turkey blocked a main road to the northern Iraqi border overnight as a cross-border military operation against the guerrillas entered its sixth day, witnesses said on Monday.
They said Kurdistan Workers Party (PKK) guerrillas set up a road block on Sunday night and set fire to two petrol tankers.
The rebels fled from the scene in Nusaybin, on the Syrian border in southeast Turkey, after making a speech in support of their cause and then opening fire on the trucks, the witnesses said.
In a separate incident, the rebels launched a rocket attack on the town of Derik in nearby Mardin province, state-run Anatolian news agency reported. It said the assault caused little damage.
The attacks came as Turkish troops backed by air power spread their search for PKK guerrillas in the mountainous border regions of Iraq in an operation which has drawn international criticism.
Ankara appealed to Tehran on Sunday to stop the rebels fleeing across the border to safety in Iranian territory.

Anatolian said a PKK camp at Zap near the border with Iran had been destroyed by troops backed by F-4 fighter planes and Cobra helicopters. It said some of the rebels were trying to escape across the border into Iran.
Correspondents were barred from the area and communications were blocked, making independent confirmation of the reports impossible.

On Monday, military officials at the Turkish Habur border crossing into northern Iraq continued to enforce a ban on journalists entering the region. Access remained limited to those with Iraqi passports.
Military sources say the rebel death toll stood at over 1,000, with around 150 guerrillas captured. They put the soldier death toll at 14.

Pro-Kurdish MED-TV said more than 30 Turkish soldiers had been killed in fighting with the rebels. It made no mention of PKK casualties in northern Iraq, but said one guerrilla had been killed in clashes with soldiers in eastern Turkey, in which 15 troops had died.
More than 22,000 people have died in the PKK's 12-year-old armed struggle for self-rule in southeast Turkey.

MED-TV said the rebels had shot down three army helicopters during the operation. Military headquarters said on Sunday an army helicopter had crashed in Iraq after a "technical fault", killing two pilots.
Western capitals and the United Nations have criticised the operation and urged Ankara to withdraw the troops and expressed worry for the safety of civilians.
